title: Minority Soldiers Leave the Ranks
narrative: The declaration of a Bosniak national state lands in the barracks. Serb and Croat soldiers who had served the Republic find the foundations shifting beneath them. A slow trickle becomes a quiet exodus — not a mutiny, but a thousand personal decisions to go home, cross the line, or simply disappear from the rolls. Recruitment officers report a noticeable cooling in the multi-ethnic towns.

effect.text: Minority soldiers quietly leave the ARBiH ranks.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 6. Reflects real 1992 ARBiH debates documented in Ramet, 'Thinking about Yugoslavia' (2005), and Burg & Shoup, 'The War in Bosnia-Herzegovina' (2000).

title: A Nation Under Siege
narrative: The identity decision hardens into resolve. By late 1993 the civic republican rhetoric has faded; the mosque, the neighborhood, and the language carry the appeal to arms. Mobilization offices see longer queues and shorter discussions. What has been lost in international legitimacy is recovered, at least for now, in the willingness of the survivors to fight.

effect.text: Bosniak ethnic solidarity powers ARBiH recruitment.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 6. Reflects the real radicalization curve inside ARBiH through 1993 documented in Hoare, 'How Bosnia Armed' (2004).

title: The World Stops Listening
narrative: Foreign mediators who once championed Sarajevo as the last multi-ethnic capital now brief their governments in a different tone. The platform has not been revoked, but the briefings about ethnic institutions and exclusive recruitment have gone back to capitals that care. The Contact Group begins preparing for a Bosnia that looks like a Bosniak entity, not a republic — and negotiates accordingly.

effect.text: International mediators treat RBiH as ethnic party, not civic state.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 6. Counterfactual mirror of Contact Group diplomatic calculus 1993-94.

title: The Pocket Falls
narrative: The 5th Corps has held against VRS, RSK, and Abdic's APWB for almost two years. The arithmetic of siege outlasts the arithmetic of defenders: no airdrops, no reinforcement road, no column of volunteers left to march in. The RBiH defensive perimeter breaks in sectors and does not close again. Refugees cross into Croatian territory by the tens of thousands. A Corps that had been a national symbol becomes a casualty list.

effect.text: The Bihac pocket collapses. 5th Corps is destroyed or captured.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 4. Counterfactual to the historical 5th Corps breakout of 1995.

title: Northwest Front Freed
narrative: With Bihac eliminated as an open wound, the VRS 2nd Krajina Corps redeploys. Fifteen to twenty brigades that had been tied down for two years walk out of the Bihac perimeter and onto trucks for central Bosnia. The strategic picture shifts faster than any single operation could ever shift it. The RS political leadership smells the end of the war — on its terms.

effect.text: VRS 2nd Krajina Corps redeploys to central Bosnia.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 4.

title: A Quarter Million on the Move
narrative: The displaced of Bihac do not stop at the first line of safety. Croatia's temporary camps overflow within weeks; the columns reach the Neretva, the Lasva, the Bosna. ARBiH supply officers compete with UNHCR for the same trucks, the same fuel, the same calories. International coverage hardens — but the people are already cold, and damage to the RBiH manpower system is already done.

effect.text: A massive refugee wave floods RBiH-held central Bosnia.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 4.

title: The Camps Are Found
narrative: Foreign journalists and ICRC delegations reach the network of detention facilities across the Prijedor and Banja Luka regions ahead of the historical ITN broadcast of 6 August 1992. With RS political leadership committed to maximum force, the chain of command around Omarska, Keraterm, and Trnopolje is less disciplined and less concealed than in the historical record. Photographs reach London, Paris, and Washington earlier; capitals that had been preparing slow responses find themselves answering morning cables. Belgrade notes, privately, that the arithmetic of plausible deniability has shifted against it.

effect.text: Detention-camp documentation reaches Western capitals weeks earlier than in the historical record.

historical_source: ICTY Stakic Trial Judgment (IT-97-24-T) and Kvocka et al. Trial Judgment (IT-98-30/1-T) on Omarska, Keraterm, and Trnopolje detention facilities; Tadic Trial Judgment (IT-94-1-T) on camp structure. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.

title: ICTY Opens Its Doors Early
narrative: The accumulating record of atrocities reaches a political threshold the Security Council cannot defer. The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia is stood up with expanded indictment authority; early subpoenas reach Pale and Belgrade. Serbian President Milosevic, calculating costs, orders a quiet pullback of logistical and personnel channels that had connected the VJ to the VRS. Karadzic and Mladic learn the shape of their defense through their lawyers, not through public argument.

effect.text: ICTY mandate expanded; Belgrade distances itself from the VRS earlier than in history.

historical_source: UNSCR 827 (25 May 1993) established the ICTY. Counterfactual: earlier and more heavily-resourced mandate in response to accumulated aggressive-goals evidence. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.

title: Safe Areas With Teeth
narrative: UNSCR 819, 824, and 836 arrive in the counterfactual with the mandate and the rules of engagement the historical resolutions lacked. Dutch and French detachments arrive at Srebrenica, Gorazde, Zepa, and Bihac with artillery and close-air-support tasking, not only with logistic and observer roles. VRS corps commanders in Drinski and eastern axes receive written guidance that operations against those perimeters will be met with NATO response. The arithmetic of the enclaves changes: they cease to be siege objectives and begin to be diplomatic preconditions.

effect.text: UN Safe Areas arrive with a defence mandate; RS operations against Bihac, Srebrenica, Gorazde, and Zepa are constrained.

historical_source: UNSCR 819 (16 April 1993) — Srebrenica safe area; UNSCR 824 (6 May 1993) — six safe areas; UNSCR 836 (4 June 1993) — defence mandate. ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T) documented that the historical mandate fell short; this counterfactual models the enforced version. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.

title: NATO Will Not Wait for Markale
narrative: Cumulative ICTY evidence and the documented shelling of civilian infrastructure drag the NATO threshold forward by more than a year. Allied Force commanders receive strike authorisations that in the historical record waited until August 1995. The VRS loses the freedom of movement it had relied on through 1994; front-line commanders begin to plan their operations around coverage windows of the no-fly zone rather than around the enemy. The war's endgame window has closed on Republika Srpska earlier than Mladic's staff had projected.

effect.text: NATO intervention threshold lowered; VRS operational freedom constrained.

historical_source: Operation Deliberate Force (30 August - 20 September 1995) was the historical turning point; counterfactual moves that threshold earlier in response to cumulative aggressive-goals evidence. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.

title: The Forests Above the Drina
narrative: The Drina valley is not cleared. Bosniak populations remain in their villages above Zvornik, Bratunac, and Vlasenica; in Foca, the town emptied during the spring has filled again from the surrounding woods. What had been civilian reservists of the Territorial Defence reconstitutes slowly, in small groups and without a clear command, but it reconstitutes. By late 1992 the VRS commands of Drinski and eastern Bosnia are reporting ambushes on supply columns and disappearances of small patrols in the high forests above the Drina.

effect.text: TDF remnants in the uncleared Drina valley begin partisan operations against VRS rear-area units.

historical_source: Counterfactual chain derived from the ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T) discussion of how Drina-valley cleansing foreclosed Bosniak military presence behind VRS lines. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 1.

title: The Corridor Costs More
narrative: The ambush pattern proves chronic. The Foca-Visegrad-Zvornik corridor, never paved and always exposed, takes losses at a rate the VRS cannot replace from a VJ whose own political calculations are shifting. Belgrade, which had sustained the VRS through 1992 on the assumption the rear was secure, begins to treat Drina logistics as a separate and more expensive problem. Convoys leave later, arrive lighter, and return with casualties.

effect.text: VRS Drina-corridor supply degrades; Belgrade adjusts its posture accordingly.

historical_source: Derived from ICTY Milosevic Trial (IT-02-54) exhibits on VJ-VRS logistics coupling. Counterfactual: cost of the coupling rises when the rear is not secured. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 1.

title: Drina Corps on Interior Lines
narrative: Drina Corps returns its quarterly readiness report with a line the VRS general staff has not seen before: more than half of the corps is committed to rear-security and anti-partisan tasks. The Podrinje Detachment is reformed and permanently redeployed from offensive tasks to interior lines. Whatever campaign Mladic's staff had projected for the eastern axis in 1993 becomes an operational impossibility; Drina Corps will hold what it has and not move from it.

effect.text: Drina Corps fixes in place on rear-security tasks; eastern-axis offensive capacity is foreclosed for the war's duration.

historical_source: Counterfactual: absent the refugee-producing cleansing, VRS Drina Corps cannot concentrate for enclave-reduction operations because rear security absorbs its manoeuvre capacity. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 1.

title: A Valley That Did Not Empty
narrative: The population remains. The villages of Srebrenica, Bratunac, and Vlasenica municipalities are not emptied; the surrounding countryside retains its pre-war demographic shape. Without the refugee waves that in the historical record flooded the enclaves and overwhelmed their garrisons, the besieged-enclave pattern does not form as it did. Srebrenica municipality continues to function as an ordinary municipality under ARBiH administration, supplied overland and contiguous with the forces defending it. Its young men reach ARBiH units through the normal mobilisation channels rather than through the wave of displaced persons.

effect.text: Drina-valley population intact; the refugee wave that in the historical record created the besieged-enclave pattern does not form.

historical_source: Counterfactual state consequence: in the absence of systematic cleansing, the enclave system that anchored the Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde siege patterns in the historical record does not emerge. Described in third-person historical voice per docs/10_canon/SENSITIVE_HISTORY_DESIGN_GATE.md §4. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 1.

title: The Enclave Holds
narrative: The enclave persists into the summer of 1995. UNPROFOR's Dutch detachment continues its patrols; RS forces continue their checkpoints and their occasional shellings. The attack that in the historical record overran the perimeter does not come. Drina Corps reports from the field describe the arithmetic frankly: a sustained final operation against the enclave is possible but would require force concentrations the corps cannot spare from its other defensive commitments. The operation is deferred, and then deferred again.

effect.text: The final operation against Srebrenica is deferred; the enclave remains under UNPROFOR protection.

historical_source: Counterfactual: the ICTY Krstic Trial (IT-98-33-T) documented the specific operational decision to reduce the enclave. This event models the world in which that decision is not taken. Per docs/10_canon/SENSITIVE_HISTORY_DESIGN_GATE.md §L60, the absence of the genocide rupture is itself the canon-legal upside; no additional standing bonus is awarded. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 3.

title: Fixed on Interior Lines
narrative: What had been assumed to be a three-month operational detour becomes a permanent commitment. The forces Drina Corps tasked against Srebrenica cannot be withdrawn without collapsing the siege perimeter, and the perimeter cannot be collapsed without either taking the enclave or withdrawing from the eastern axis. Neither option is available. The formations remain in place: fixed, frustrated, and unavailable to the wider war.

effect.text: Drina Corps is fixed in place on its siege tasking and cannot redeploy.

historical_source: Counterfactual: when the enclave is not reduced, Drina Corps retains the rear-area fixing it had in the spring of 1995 without the operational release the historical July offensive provided. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 3.

title: The Case Assembles Without Srebrenica
narrative: The case for sustained NATO air operations over Bosnia is assembled from the evidence the war has produced rather than from a single catalysing atrocity. Markale's shelling, the accumulated ICTY record, the hostage crisis of May, the repositioning of the Rapid Reaction Force — the arguments line up differently without the fall of Srebrenica, and they line up more slowly, but they line up. Brussels, Paris, and Washington coordinate the plan that the historical record assembled around the massacre. It takes longer. It arrives with less political momentum. It arrives.

effect.text: Deliberate Force triggers from cumulative war-crimes evidence, Markale, and RRF deployment rather than from Srebrenica.

historical_source: The historiographical debate about whether Srebrenica was the trigger or the accelerant for Deliberate Force is treated in Power, 'A Problem from Hell' (2002), and Holbrooke, 'To End a War' (1998). Counterfactual models the non-Srebrenica catalyst stack. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 3.

title: A Fourth Summer
narrative: Three summers of war without the turning point that in the historical record closed it. Populations in Sarajevo, Banja Luka, and Mostar cross into the fourth year of casualty lists, shortages, and negotiations that settle nothing. Conscription offices on every side report longer queues for deferments and shorter ones at the intake desk. This is not judgement; it is exhaustion. Every faction's field army is holding the line it held in the spring, and every faction's politicians are having the same conversations in different cities about how a war this expensive ends.

effect.text: Without a decisive catalyst, the war enters its fourth summer as emergent exhaustion rather than resolution.

historical_source: Counterfactual: absent the Deliberate Force catalyst, the war continues with the pattern of exhaustion Burg & Shoup, 'The War in Bosnia-Herzegovina' (2000), describe for late 1994. Framed as emergent war-weariness per docs/10_canon/SENSITIVE_HISTORY_DESIGN_GATE.md §7 principle 3. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 3.

title: Joint Operations, Formalized
narrative: The agreement is signed at Mostar in late spring. HVO and ARBiH commands formalise what has been a working reality in parts of central Bosnia since winter: joint staff liaison at the operational level, combined defensive planning against the VRS, mutual supply arrangements through Split and Ploce. In Zagreb, Defence Minister Susak reads the English-language summary and sets it aside with a look his staff have learned to recognise. In Sarajevo and Mostar, the officers who will have to keep the agreement going read the Bosnian and Croatian summaries and believe at least some of it.

effect.text: HVO-ARBiH joint operations agreement signed; alliance locked at or above 0.50 for the agreement's operational life.

historical_source: Counterfactual: the Split Agreement of July 1992 between Tudjman and Izetbegovic is treated in Burg & Shoup, 'The War in Bosnia-Herzegovina' (2000), as a moment when a sustained united-front path was diplomatically available. This event models the trajectory in which that path is taken. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 2.

title: Susak's Quiet Adjustment
narrative: Through the early months of 1993 the cargo manifests from Split arrive in Herzegovina with fewer pallets than the autumn's planning had assumed. Ministers in Zagreb who had briefed Tudjman on a Croat entity within Bosnia now brief him on a junior partnership inside someone else's republic, and his response is to let the supply arithmetic speak the policy. HVO brigades draw on smaller stocks, replace equipment more slowly, and discover which of their depot arrangements were built on Zagreb's priorities and which on their own.

effect.text: Zagreb reduces logistical support for HVO; HRHB supply degrades.

historical_source: Counterfactual: ICTY Prlic et al. Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T) on Zagreb-HRHB resource flows. When the HRHB political direction does not match Zagreb's preferences, the documented supply coupling weakens. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 2.

title: Who Administers Central Bosnia
narrative: The alliance does not end; the arguments begin. In Travnik, Zenica, Bugojno, Vitez, Gornji Vakuf — the towns that make up central Bosnia — HVO commanders and ARBiH commanders coexist in practice and negotiate in committee. Committees sit longer. By summer the question of which civilian administration signs requisitions, which police collect taxes, which schools open in which language, and whose flag flies over which building has produced a paper trail that the soldiers quietly curse. None of it is fighting. All of it is tension the alliance has to absorb.

effect.text: Administrative friction in mixed-population central Bosnian municipalities strains the united-front alliance.

historical_source: Counterfactual: the real-world friction over central Bosnia administration documented in the ICTY Kordic Trial Judgment (IT-95-14/2-T) is, in the ahistorical united-front path, contained within alliance politics rather than spilling into open war. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 2.

title: Federation Before Washington
narrative: The agreement that in the historical record required American pressure and the threat of NATO sanctions on all sides arrives on its own timetable. The united-front soldiers have held a common line against the VRS for the better part of two years; the politicians who follow their lead sign a federation structure that codifies what the armies already practise. The text owes less to the State Department and more to the working arrangements of central Bosnia. It is not the Washington Agreement that the historical record produced. It is an earlier, leaner document that leaves some questions deliberately open because the signatories trust each other enough to come back to them.

effect.text: An early Federation forms without the Washington Agreement's coercive pressure.

historical_source: Counterfactual: Holbrooke, 'To End a War' (1998), describes the Washington Agreement (1 March 1994) as an American-pressured settlement of an open war. This event models the earlier, softer Federation that the documentary record suggests was diplomatically available if the 1993 Croat-Bosniak war had not occurred. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 2.

title: The Combined Spring
narrative: With the federation structure in place and Zagreb no longer attempting to fight a parallel war, HVO and ARBiH commands coordinate the offensive planning of spring 1994 as a single operational matter. Combined staffs assemble at Zenica and Mostar; supply and evacuation are run from a shared rear. The operations that the historical record fragmented across competing axes — the Kupres-Grahovo direction, the central Bosnia corridor, the pressure on the Posavina bulge — are now pursued together. The VRS's intelligence cells, which had relied on the Croat-Bosniak rupture to predict where force would land, lose that predictor.

effect.text: Combined HVO-ARBiH spring offensive; aggression modifier +0.10 for both federation factions.

historical_source: Counterfactual: the operations of 1994 (Operation Tiger, Maslenica carryover, Kupres area) occurred in the historical record despite the recent Croat-Bosniak war and with fragile coordination. This event models what combined operational staffs would plausibly accomplish without that rupture. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 2.

title: Ahmici and the Rupture
narrative: On 16 April 1993 the HVO Viteska Brigade enters Ahmici at dawn. The village burns before the day is out; 116 civilians are killed in the operation. From that morning onward the alliance that had existed on paper for ten months is a written fiction and the war between HVO and ARBiH is a matter of specific coordinates. Mate Boban's Herceg-Bosna pursues the Banovina-border programme it had always intended; Zagreb's material support, which had been hedged under the joint-front arrangement, flows more openly. Viteska, Busovaca, and the Nikola Subic-Zrinski brigades move against ARBiH positions in the Lasva and Neretva valleys. The arithmetic is simple: the HVO has the initiative for a season, and it will use it.

effect.text: HVO initiates the Croat-Bosniak war; alliance with ARBiH collapses; central-Bosnia offensive begins.

historical_source: ICTY Kordic Trial Judgment (IT-95-14/2-T) on the Ahmici massacre of 16 April 1993 and the Lasva Valley operations. ICTY Prlic et al. Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T) on Zagreb-HRHB command coupling. Per war-or-game + corps-army-commander design consult 2026-04-23: the event must break the RBiH-HRHB alliance (floor below hostility threshold), bump HVO morale/cohesion to un-stick combat-readiness, and shift offensive priorities to central-Bosnia municipalities. Phase 2 (ARBiH counter-offensive, three-enclave defensive posture) emerges organically via normal ARBiH offensive doctrine once alliance is locked hostile. Issue #9.

title: An Alliance That Did Not Break
narrative: The Mostar guns never opened up. The Ahmici road never burned. Past week thirty-five — the date the historians had circled — the RBiH-HRHB alliance is still functioning. The Washington table the Americans imagined is now a different table: not a cease-fire forced on belligerents, but a coordination of two fronts that never split. Cohesion in the joint sectors holds.

effect.text: RBiH-HRHB alliance survives past w35; Washington alt-path opens.

historical_source: Divergence Ring 1 (LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-ROUND2-DIVERGENCE-EVENT-SEEDS). Counter-historical: an unbroken RBiH-HRHB alliance past the historical April-1993 rupture window, anchored to alliance > 0.20 and absence of war flags. /narrative-designer + /historian sign-off.

title: The Sweep That Was Never Ordered
narrative: Twenty turns and counting. The political files do not contain the order. The paramilitary detachments that, on other timelines, would have been turned loose on the rear-area municipalities are still confined to peripheral roles. The international monitors cite a clean record. It is the rarest commodity in this war: a ledger without massacres.

effect.text: No paramilitary authorization for 20+ turns; clean-record divergence.

historical_source: Divergence Ring 1 (LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-ROUND2-DIVERGENCE-EVENT-SEEDS). Models the counter-historical case where rear-area paramilitary authorization is withheld for 20+ turns. /narrative-designer + /historian sign-off.

title: Safe Areas Still Standing
narrative: By turn 145 the enclaves are not the museum exhibits the world expected to inspect after the fact. Resilience indices are running well above the floor. The columns have not marched out. The lists have not been compiled. The UN Safe Areas designation, which on the historical path became a euphemism for unfinished obligation, is still — for now — an enforced reality.

effect.text: Enclaves intact past t145; alt-intervention path annotated.

effects.text: UN Safe Areas designation enforced past t145 — counter-historical alt-intervention path.

historical_source: Divergence Ring 1 (LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-ROUND2-DIVERGENCE-EVENT-SEEDS). Audit-only: does NOT flip genocide_condemnation. Counter-historical preservation of the eastern enclaves through t145. /narrative-designer + /historian sign-off.

title: Three Times No
narrative: The patron's envoy returned three times with three different demands and left three times empty-handed. The cables back to the capital described a client increasingly difficult to steer. The cost will not be free: arms shipments are reviewed, training rotations slip, and the recruitment networks that depended on the patron's good will begin to thin. But the principle has been established.

effect.text: Three or more patron resist responses; patron confidence and recruitment penalty applied.

historical_source: Divergence Ring 1 (LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-ROUND2-DIVERGENCE-EVENT-SEEDS). Streak counter `patron_resist_streak` is incremented by patron-event response options. Faction-agnostic predicate; effects target the resisting faction (authored RS by default; alt-faction variants can be added downstream).

title: Pen Before the Last Offensive
narrative: The plan is signed before the last offensive runs its course. The ink is dry and the cease-fire boundary is drawn while several axes still have momentum and several enclaves are still intact. The leverage that the late-war battles would have purchased never materializes; what is on the table now is what will be on the table at the final accord. The negotiators understand the trade.

effect.text: Peace accepted before t120 with non-baseline territory; leverage floor locked, ledger annotated.

effects.text: Peace plan accepted before t120 with territorial position outside late-war baseline. Leverage trade recorded.

historical_source: Divergence Ring 1 (LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-ROUND2-DIVERGENCE-EVENT-SEEDS). Late-war baseline territorial position approximated by RS area share <0.62 (Dayton-era anchor). Audit-only ledger annotation; no rupture wiring.

title: The Inverted Roster
narrative: The officer rolls tell the story the front line had begun to suspect. The veteran cadre on the historically dominant side has thinned past the inflection point — not from any single battle, but from accumulation: postings refused, replacements thinned, the senior class retiring into silence. On the other side, new commanders cycle through hard schools and come out the other end. The predictor's confidence in the old assumptions takes a small but real haircut.

effect.text: RS officer-quality average has fallen below ARBiH and dropped >0.15 from baseline.

historical_source: Divergence Ring 1 (LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-ROUND2-DIVERGENCE-EVENT-SEEDS). Static baseline 0.55 reflects scenario-init RS officer_quality (CALIBRATION_MASTER, Memory 'officer quality faction defaults'). Faction-agnostic predicate authored with RS<-RBiH for the historical dominant-side; alt orientations can be added downstream. Predictor-confidence haircut consumed via the `predictor_confidence_haircut` flag.

title: The Silent Drift
narrative: No declaration, no incident — the alliance simply thins. Joint patrols stop coordinating. Liaison officers are reassigned without replacements. The press communiqués grow shorter. By any measurable count the partnership still exists; in the practice of it the trust has gone elsewhere. Capitals on both sides note the change and adjust their expectations downward.

effect.text: RBiH-HRHB cooperation thins without an open break.

effects.text: RBiH-HRHB cooperation drifted below 0.40 with measurable recent erosion; ceiling-locked for 30 turns.

historical_source: LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-CONSEQUENCE-BREADTH (alliance/diplomacy A1). Predicate uses additive `alliance_drift` condition kind. Faction-agnostic; alliance is intrinsically RBiH-HRHB. Mirrors pre-Croat-Bosniak-war 1992-1993 erosion documented in Burg & Shoup (2000) and CIA 'Balkan Battlegrounds' I p.157-160.

title: The Joint Command Comes Apart
narrative: What had been signed on paper at Sarajevo and reaffirmed in Mostar is now, at the working level, a fiction. Shared objectives are dropped from operational orders. Liaison teams pack their files. The supply ledgers — once cross-credited between corps — are returned to single accounts. The collapse is administrative before it is military, but the military follows.

effect.text: Joint RBiH-HRHB command structure is unwound.

effects.text: Joint RBiH-HRHB operations agreement collapsed; shared objectives stripped for 20 turns.

historical_source: LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-CONSEQUENCE-BREADTH (alliance/diplomacy A2). Floor lock at -1.0 effectively clears any prior alliance_lock floor (overriding instead of mutating). Mirrors the operational collapse of HVO-ARBiH cooperation winter 1992-1993.

title: Separate Peace Overture
narrative: A back-channel draft circulates from one capital to the other, and to the mediators. The terms are bilateral. The other partner is not in the room. Negotiating leverage shifts to the faction that holds the initiative; the partner left outside notes the precedent.

effect.text: One faction quietly offers a separate peace; the other is not in the room.

effects.text: Bilateral peace overture circulated under flag_equals(peace_plan_offered) with acceptance-gap >=25.

response_options.label: Decline; keep the partnership intact
response_options.description: Hold the alliance line; refuse the bilateral track.

effects.text: Bilateral overture declined; alliance partnership preserved.

historical_source: LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-CONSEQUENCE-BREADTH (alliance/diplomacy A3). Decision event; bot uses strategic_weighted. Mirrors back-channel patterns around Vance-Owen and Owen-Stoltenberg negotiations 1993.

title: Cooperation Returns
narrative: After the hostility recedes the practical reasons for working together return faster than the trust does. Joint patrols are scheduled tentatively, then routinely. Mediators note quiet visits between capitals. Neither side calls it a revival; both sides act as if the partnership had never quite been retired.

effect.text: RBiH-HRHB cooperation reasserts itself after a hostile interlude.

effects.text: Alliance recovered above 0.30 after a prior low-water mark <0.10; floor-locked at 0.20 for 20 turns.

historical_source: LANE-NIGHTSHIFT-CONSEQUENCE-BREADTH (alliance/diplomacy A4). Mirrors the Washington Agreement / Federation rebuild pattern of 1994. The `alliance_low_water_mark_below_0_10` flag is the existing watermark counter set by alliance_update.ts.

title: The Arms Review Comes Down
narrative: The patron has run out of patient briefings. A formal arms review is announced — not a cutoff, but a procedural slowdown that reaches every depot and every transit lane. Mobilization officers will spend the next quarter explaining missing inventories. The message is clear: comply or be cut.

title: Partial Disavowal
narrative: The patron stops short of a public break — but the formal language hardens. Diplomatic representatives in capitals abroad are pulled back; sanctions cooperation widens; the public statements draw a careful distance. International standing improves on one side, declines on the other. The flow of arms and recruits both feel the chill.

title: Patron Recovery Offer
narrative: The patron's emissary returns with terms: structural concessions in exchange for a managed recovery of the relationship. Acceptance buys back arms, briefings, and the soft cover of recognized backing. Refusal locks in the disavowal. Either way the choice is binding for the rest of the war.

title: Industrial Conscription Wave
narrative: The exhaustion of the front pushes the rear into emergency mobilization. Factories release their reserved categories. Universities suspend exemptions. The recruitment numbers climb sharply for a quarter, but the bills come quickly: cohesion frays, draft evasion rises, and the decision is registered in the political truth of the war.

title: Demobilization Pressure Wave
narrative: After a quiet quarter the families return to the streets and the patron capitals add their voice. The mobilization order is not formally rescinded; it is, in practice, walked back. Recruitment offices reduce quotas. Aggressive doctrine is shelved in favor of holding. The war does not end; it slows.

title: Grain Corridor Reopened
narrative: A long-disused supply lane reopens — quietly, through municipal-level arrangements that the formal war has not abolished. Convoys move under flag-of-grain, and the receiving towns count the difference in markets that begin to function again. The international observers note the change with cautious approval.

title: Refugee Absorption Strain
narrative: The numbers cross a threshold that the receiving faction's institutions have been warning about for months. Camps overspill into rented housing; municipal budgets divert from war administration to bread and shelter. The international press reports sympathetically. The internal politics splits between solidarity and exhaustion, and the cohesion of the absorbing side erodes by the same measure.

title: Weapons Embargo Partially Lifted
narrative: Pressure from Washington and the Contact Group cracks the UN arms embargo. Channels that had been informal — Iranian flights through Croatia, Saudi cash, the Pakistani pipeline — are tacitly normalized. Trainers arrive. Equipment that was previously smuggled now arrives by manifest. The embargo on paper survives; the embargo in fact does not.

title: The Separate Track Recovers
narrative: After a quarter of cold cooperation the working channels reopen. No new agreement is signed; the existing one is simply allowed to function. Liaison desks fill again. Joint sector reports begin to circulate. The trust does not return to what it was; the working partnership does. Capitals on both sides record the change without comment.

title: The Alliance Resets
narrative: After many months at the floor the alliance is, in effect, a new agreement. The hostile chapter is closed; what comes after is uncoded. Capitals neither celebrate nor recriminate. The negotiating positions are redrawn. Whatever the partnership becomes from this point will not be a continuation of what came before.

title: Tripartite Federation Proposal
narrative: An ambitious draft circulates through three capitals: not a peace plan but a constitutional one. A federation of three communities, each with autonomy, each with a veto, none with a majority. The mediators see in it the only structural answer to the war's grammar; the parties see in it whatever each side most fears or most wants. The decision is not whether the proposal is good — it is whether to keep the door open.

narrative: The shipment that had been delayed in customs and renamed in cables finally arrives. Crates marked humanitarian unload as artillery; rifles arrive in numbers the embargo paperwork does not acknowledge. The patron's investment in the war becomes, briefly, a measurable thing. Combat units rotate through the depot and emerge measurably better-armed.

title: The Tribunal Files Its Notice
narrative: An international observation team files a formal notice — not yet an indictment, not yet a sealed file, but the formal recording of attention. Patterns are catalogued. Names appear in working documents. The political truth of the war moves a small notch toward the courtroom. The faction in question registers the change in its standing without public comment.

title: The Quiet Channel
narrative: The official supply lanes are constrained; the unofficial ones are not. A municipal-level network — drivers, brokers, customs officers willing to look elsewhere — moves what the formal logistics cannot. The general supply reserve climbs noticeably for a quarter. The cost is a small but measurable cohesion drain: the political truth of the war is that the rear is becoming a market, not a state.

title: The Camps Provide Hands
narrative: The refugee camps in the receiving territory have been counted and re-counted; now they are surveyed. Working-age men and women from the displaced register are organized into labor brigades — for trench-digging, for road repair, for harvests under the war. The recruitment pool widens by the same amount that the rear-area cohesion thins. The bargain is registered.

title: The Last Wave
narrative: The recruitment offices that had grown quiet for a quarter see queues again. The cause is not patriotic so much as territorial: the loss of one more municipality has crossed a threshold. Older men sign on. Veterans who had been demobilized return. The wave is short — these are not new bodies, they are the last available ones — but it buys a season.

The numbers are real but the cohesion is brittle: these are not the volunteers, they are the called. The recruitment columns rise; the morale columns thin. title: The Partition Question
narrative: A draft proposal circulates in three languages. It does not name a settlement — it names a question, to be put to the populations. The mediators frame it as legitimacy; the parties read it as either a foothold or a precipice. The decision is whether the question gets asked at all. Refusal is a posture; engagement is, in its own way, an answer the parties have not given before.

title: The Pipeline Goes Quiet
narrative: The route that had supplied a quarter of the heavy munitions stops moving. Embargoes tighten at one customs post; a brokered shipment is impounded at another. There is no announcement — the absence is the announcement. Combat units rotating through the depot find the manifests thin. The shortfall registers as a small but durable downgrade in firepower, and the recruitment offices feel the shift before the front does.

title: The Captured Stockpile
narrative: A successful operation closes around a depot that had been counted in the other faction's order of battle for two years. Crates marked in foreign cyrillic, vehicles still in factory paint, ammunition in calibers the receiving side had been rationing — all of it inventoried by the captors and rotated out within the month. The combat-power uplift is short, but it is real. The losing side's manifests register the gap.

title: The Manifests Run Clean
narrative: After the agreement the arms paperwork that had been laundered through humanitarian cover or quietly looked-past begins running through proper customs. The headline numbers do not change much; the reliability does. Spare parts arrive on schedule. Calibres that had been rationed appear in adequate quantities. The change is bureaucratic, not heroic, but the depots register it and the front follows by the second quarter.

The reform is partial — the war has not stopped — but the institution upgrades visibly. Recruitment offices report an uplift in volunteer quality; the existing ranks register the improvement in cohesion within a quarter.
